modifications: Capability and cost evaluation only; no Godot code is copied or translated.

TAA (taa.h): resolve() requires depth, velocity, previous velocity and history textures plus camera jitter. Rejected: the graph has no motion-vector buffer, authored trail/feedback nodes are deliberate temporal effects that jitter would fight, and W1.5a already rejected velocity reprojection for the 2D texture chain.

FSR 1.0 (fsr.cpp): spatial two-pass upscaler (EASU + RCAS), an upscaling/performance feature rather than native-resolution antialiasing. Deferred to the final platform stage as an Android performance candidate, not an AA path.
FSR 2 (fsr2.h): temporal upscaler requiring depth, velocity and reactive mask inputs through multiple passes. Rejected for the same motion-vector dependency as TAA.

SMAA (smaa.h): three passes (edge detection with stencil, weight calculation with precomputed area/search lookup textures, blending). Better thin-line geometry preservation than FXAA, recorded as the candidate upgrade if an authored work demonstrates FXAA line softening as a defect.

MSAA: render-target sample counts only help rasterized geometry edges and require resolve before sampling; the dominant aliasing source in authored works is texture-chain content (noise, trails, glow), which MSAA cannot touch. No authored work currently shows 3D mesh edge aliasing, so no MSAA target is introduced.

Decision: keep the per-node opt-in FXAA as the shipped AA path; the moving thin-line/particle comparison (windows_aa_motion_gpu) quantifies its softening and confirms temporal flicker persists, matching the audit expectation.
